content: Possible side effects of this medication include drowsiness, dizziness, constipation, stomach upset, blurred vision, and dryness of the mouth, nose, or throat. If your doctor has prescribed this medication, it is because they have determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not a complete list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance regarding side effects. Precautions: Before using diphenhydramine, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to dimenhydrinate, or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, drowsiness, or blurred vision. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. Liquid products, chewable tablets, or dissolving tablets/strips may contain sugar and/or aspartame. Liquid forms may also contain alcohol. Use caution if you have diabetes, liver disease, phenylketonuria (PKU), or any condition requiring dietary restrictions of these substances. Children may be more sensitive to the side effects of this drug. Older adults may also be more susceptible to side effects such as drowsiness, dizziness, confusion, constipation, or difficulty urinating. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. Diphenhydramine passes into breast milk and may have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Check the labels of all your medications (e.g., allergy or cough-and-cold products) as they may contain ingredients that cause drowsiness. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests (e.g., allergy skin tests), potentially leading to false results. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Symptoms of overdose may include severe drowsiness, seizures, or widened pupils. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is near the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Storage: Store this medication at room temperature, away from moisture and light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not freeze liquid forms of this medication. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not contain all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individual medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
